question: If sin θ = √3 cos θ, then what is the value of (3sin ² theta +cos theta)/(2cos theta +5)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: **sin θ = √3 cos θ** ⇒ **tan θ = √3**.

For tan θ = √3, the value of **θ = 60°**.

Substitute θ = 60° in the expression: (3 sin² 60° + cos 60°) ÷ (2 cos 60° + 5).

⇒ [3 × (3/4) + 1/2] ÷ [2 × (1/2) + 5] = (9/4 + 2/4) ÷ (1 + 5) = (11/4) ÷ 6 = 11/24.

**∴ The correct answer is 11/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac4286159e7fec1ebbbac9631f59f20eb2a0ee36523d13ced0b0579ac44e0434.png] 

**Given:** sin θ = √3 cos θ ⇒ sin θ / cos θ = √3 ⇒ tan θ = √3 / 1

**Formula Used:** tan θ = p/b | h = √(p² + b²) | sin θ = p/h | cos θ = b/h

⇒ p = √3, b = 1 ∴ h = √((√3)² + 1²) = √(3 + 1) = 2

⇒ sin θ = √3 / 2 and cos θ = 1 / 2

⇒ Value = [3 × (√3/2)² + (1/2)] ÷ [2 × (1/2) + 5]

⇒ Value = [3 × (3/4) + 1/2] ÷ [1 + 5]

⇒ Value = [9/4 + 2/4] ÷ 6 = (11/4) ÷ 6 = 11/24

**∴ The correct answer is 11/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental relations: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Specific Angles

Standard values: sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3.

Right Angled Triangle Properties

Pythagoras theorem states that Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².</p
